1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	"""Stage 00 — create a project and register its raw data.
3	
4	The deterministic core of `00_initialize_project`. The contract orchestrates; this computes.
5	See docs/decisions/0011-deterministic-artifacts-in-stages-00-01.md for why.
6	
7	This script decides what is TRUE. It never prompts, never links without being told the user
8	confirmed, and never invents a sample ID it cannot derive. The agent decides what to say and
9	when to stop.
10	
11	Stdlib only, and verified on stock python 3.6.8: stages 00 and 01 must run with no conda
12	environment, unlike stage 02.
13	
14	The four subcommands are the contract's own phases, so a conversation turn sits between each:
15	
16	    assays    steps 3-6    offer the supported assays; resolve a selection -> backs T3
17	    create    step  7      sanitize the title, validate assays, copy the stamp
18	    inspect   step  9      read-only scan of one source directory   -> backs T4a
19	    link      step  12     symlink one assay's raw files            -> backs T4b
20	    finalize  steps 14-19  metadata, placeholders, exit gate        -> backs T6 / T9
21	
22	Every subcommand emits a single JSON object on stdout. Exit codes:
23	
24	    0  ok
25	    1  failure; report and stop (T9)
26	    2  refused; the JSON's `template` field names which reply to send (T5 / T7 / T8)
27	    3  usage or precondition error
28	
29	Note on cost: `finalize` defaults to `--integrity quick` -- resolves, non-empty, gzip magic --
30	because at this stage EVERY registered file would be verified, including the ones the user is
31	about to exclude at the 00 -> 01 gate. Deep verification of the files that will actually be
32	analysed belongs to stage 01, which is the first moment the included subset exists. `--integrity
33	full` is still available here and still honest about what it did: the mode is stamped into the
34	project's HISTORY.md, never assumed.
35	"""
36	
37	import argparse
38	import csv
39	import datetime
40	import json
41	import os
42	import re
43	import sys
44	from pathlib import Path

46	sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
47	import integrity            # noqa: E402  -- one home for the integrity rule
48	import workspace as ws     # noqa: E402  -- one home for the template version

50	RAW_SUFFIXES = (".fastq.gz", ".fq.gz", ".fastq", ".fq")
51	FILES_HEADER = ["sample_id", "lane", "fastq_1", "fastq_2"]
52	BCL2FASTQ = re.compile(r"^(?P<sample>.+?)_S\d+_(?:L(?P<lane>\d+)_)?R(?P<read>[12])_\d+\."
53	                       r"(?:fastq|fq)(?:\.gz)?$")
54	
55	EXIT_OK, EXIT_FAILURE, EXIT_REFUSED, EXIT_USAGE = 0, 1, 2, 3
56	
57	
58	def emit(result, code):
59	    json.dump(result, sys.stdout, indent=2, sort_keys=True)
60	    sys.stdout.write("\n")
61	    return code

65	
66	def sanitize_title(title):
67	    """Contract: keep [A-Za-z0-9_-]; space -> _; drop the rest; collapse _; strip leading/trailing
68	    _ and -."""
69	    s = title.replace(" ", "_")
70	    s = "".join(c for c in s if re.match(r"[A-Za-z0-9_-]", c))
71	    s = re.sub(r"_+", "_", s)
72	    return s.strip("_-")
73	
74	
75	def read_assay_map(workspace):
76	    """Parse the Assay / Assay ID columns of the FIRST table headed `| Assay | Assay ID |`.
77	
78	    Binding to that header matters: the file holds a second table (Skill requirements) whose
79	    first two columns are Skill / Python. Reading every pipe-prefixed line accepted `rnaseq-de`
80	    as an assay and created a directory named `(unpinned)` from the Python column.
81	    """
82	    path = workspace / "_references" / "assay_stage_skill_map.md"
83	    if not path.is_file():
84	        return None, "assay map not found at %s" % path
85	
86	    catalog, in_table = {}, False
87	    for line in path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
88	        stripped = line.strip()
89	        if not stripped.startswith("|"):
90	            if in_table:
91	                break          # the table ended; never read past it
92	            continue
93	        cells = [c.strip() for c in stripped.strip("|").split("|")]
94	        if len(cells) < 2:
95	            continue
96	        if not in_table:
97	            if cells[0] == "Assay" and cells[1] == "Assay ID":
98	                in_table = True
99	            continue
100	        if set("".join(cells[:2])) <= set("-: "):
101	            continue           # the header separator row
102	        name, aid = cells[0], cells[1]
103	        entry = catalog.setdefault(aid, {"assay": name, "substages": []})
104	        # One row per sub-stage, in the order the map lists them -- that order IS the pipeline.
105	        if len(cells) >= 5 and cells[3]:
106	            entry["substages"].append({"substage": cells[3], "skill": cells[4]})
107	
108	    if not catalog:
109	        return None, "assay map has no table headed `| Assay | Assay ID |`"
110	    return catalog, None
111	
112	
113	def catalog_names(catalog):
114	    """{assay_id: display name} -- what the matching and placeholder code needs."""
115	    return {aid: e["assay"] for aid, e in catalog.items()}
116	
117	
118	def menu(catalog):
119	    """The offer list. Numbers are PRESENTATION ONLY.
120	
121	    They are assigned from a deterministic sort of the Assay IDs and are regenerated on every
122	    call, so the numbering handed out is always the numbering `--select` resolves against. They
123	    are never written to disk, never recorded in HISTORY.md, and never used as a directory name:
124	    add an assay and `02` becomes a different thing, so a persisted number would silently rot.
125	    The Assay ID is the durable identifier and the only one that leaves this function.
126	    """
127	    return [{"n": "%02d" % i, "assay": catalog[aid]["assay"], "assay_id": aid,
128	             "substages": catalog[aid]["substages"]}
129	            for i, aid in enumerate(sorted(catalog), start=1)]
130	
131	
132	def normalize_assay(text):
133	    """Case-fold and drop every non-alphanumeric character.
134	
135	    `rnaseq-bulk`, `rnaseq_bulk`, `RNAseq Bulk` and `rnaseq bulk` all normalise to `rnaseqbulk`;
136	    `Bulk RNA-seq` and `bulk rna seq` both to `bulkrnaseq`. This is normalisation, NOT fuzzy
137	    matching -- no edit distance, no substring, no stemming. Two different assays cannot collide
138	    unless their names differ only in punctuation, which `resolve_assays` refuses outright rather
139	    than guessing between.
140	
141	    The strict version of this rejected `rnaseq-bulk` -- one character away from the Assay ID it
142	    obviously meant -- and told the user only that "Bulk RNA-seq" was supported, without ever
143	    showing the ID. Refusing a punctuation variant is not safety, it is a dead end.
144	    """
145	    return "".join(c for c in text.lower() if c.isalnum())
146	
147	
148	def resolve_assays(requested, assay_map):
149	    """Match each request against the Assay column or the Assay ID column, after normalisation.
150	
151	    Returns one entry per request. An unmatched request is reported, never resolved to a
152	    neighbour: the point of refusing is that a wrong assay silently creates the wrong pipeline.
153	    """
154	    index = {}
155	    for aid, name in assay_map.items():
156	        for form in (aid, name):
157	            index.setdefault(normalize_assay(form), set()).add(aid)
158	
159	    out = []
160	    for req in requested:
161	        key = normalize_assay(req)
162	        hits = index.get(key, set())
163	        if len(hits) == 1:
164	            out.append({"requested": req, "assay_id": sorted(hits)[0], "supported": True})
165	        elif len(hits) > 1:
166	            out.append({"requested": req, "assay_id": None, "supported": False,
167	                        "ambiguous_between": sorted(hits),
168	                        "note": "matches more than one assay; name it by Assay ID"})
169	        else:
170	            out.append({"requested": req, "assay_id": None, "supported": False})
171	    return out
172

174	def template_version(workspace):
175	    return ws.template_version(workspace)

178	# A Space Ranger output tree may arrive as a directory or as a tarball of one; the pipeline
179	# accepts either (spatialvi docs/usage.md).
180	SAMPLE_DIR_SUFFIXES = (".tar.gz", ".tgz")
181

183	def find_raw(source, kind="fastq"):
184	    """Raw input at the TOP LEVEL only. Never descends -- the contract forbids searching.
185	
186	    `fastq`: files with an NGS suffix. `sample_dir`: one directory (or tarball of one) per
187	    sample, which is how spatial data arrives -- there are no FASTQs to see.
188	    """
189	    raw, other = [], []
190	    for p in sorted(source.iterdir()):
191	        if kind == "sample_dir":
192	            is_input = p.is_dir() or p.name.endswith(SAMPLE_DIR_SUFFIXES)
193	        else:
194	            if not p.is_file() and not p.is_symlink():
195	                continue
196	            is_input = p.name.endswith(RAW_SUFFIXES)
197	        (raw if is_input else other).append(p.name)
198	    return raw, other

201	def derive_units(filenames, pattern=None, kind="fastq"):
202	    """Group filenames into (sample_id, lane) units.
203	
204	    Returns (units, layout, problems). `pattern` overrides the bcl2fastq convention and must
205	    provide named groups `sample` and `read`, optionally `lane` -- it is how the contract feeds
206	    back an answer the user gave when filenames do not match the convention.
207	
208	    For `sample_dir` there is nothing to parse and nothing to pair: each entry IS a sample, its
209	    id is the entry name with any tarball suffix removed, and the layout is reported as
210	    `sample-dir` so callers never apply a pairing rule that has no meaning here.
211	    """
212	    if kind == "sample_dir":
213	        units, problems = {}, []
214	        for name in filenames:
215	            sample = name
216	            for suffix in SAMPLE_DIR_SUFFIXES:
217	                if sample.endswith(suffix):
218	                    sample = sample[:-len(suffix)]
219	                    break
220	            if not sample:
221	                problems.append(name)
222	                continue
223	            if (sample, "") in units:
224	                problems.append(name)
225	                continue
226	            units[(sample, "")] = {"dir": name}
227	        return ({}, None, problems) if problems else (units, "sample-dir", [])
228	
229	    rx = re.compile(pattern) if pattern else BCL2FASTQ
230	    units, problems = {}, []
231	    for name in filenames:
232	        m = rx.match(name)
233	        if not m:
234	            problems.append(name)
235	            continue
236	        gd = m.groupdict()
237	        sample = gd.get("sample")
238	        lane = gd.get("lane") or ""
239	        read = gd.get("read") or "1"
240	        if not sample:
241	            problems.append(name)
242	            continue
243	        lane = "L%s" % lane if lane and not lane.startswith("L") else lane
244	        units.setdefault((sample, lane), {})[read] = name
245	
246	    if problems:
247	        return {}, None, problems
248	
249	    r2 = [u for u in units.values() if "2" in u]
250	    if len(r2) == len(units):
251	        layout = "paired-end"
252	    elif not r2:
253	        layout = "single-end"
254	    else:
255	        layout = "mixed"
256	    return units, layout, []
257	
258	
259	def units_to_rows(units, assay_id, kind="fastq"):
260	    """Rows for files.csv, shaped by the assay's input kind (workspace.FILES_HEADERS)."""
261	    rows = []
262	    base = "00_data/%s/raw/" % assay_id
263	    if kind == "sample_dir":
264	        for (sample, _) in sorted(units):
265	            rows.append([sample, base + units[(sample, "")]["dir"]])
266	        return rows
267	    for (sample, lane) in sorted(units):
268	        reads = units[(sample, lane)]
269	        rows.append([sample, lane,
270	                     base + reads["1"] if "1" in reads else "",
271	                     base + reads["2"] if "2" in reads else ""])
272	    return rows
273

277	def cmd_assays(args, workspace):
278	    """Offer the supported assays, and resolve a selection back to Assay IDs.
279	
280	    Two modes, one source of truth. Without --select it returns the menu the agent renders; with
281	    --select it resolves what the user picked. Both derive from the same `menu()` call, so the
282	    numbering offered cannot drift from the numbering accepted.
283	
284	    A selection may name a number (`01`), an Assay ID, or a display name -- whatever the user
285	    typed. Everything resolves to Assay IDs, and only Assay IDs are returned.
286	    """
287	    result = {"command": "assays", "ok": False}
288	    catalog, err = read_assay_map(workspace)
289	    if err:
290	        result["error"] = err
291	        return emit(result, EXIT_USAGE)
292	
293	    offered = menu(catalog)
294	    result["assays"] = offered
295	
296	    if args.select is None:
297	        result["ok"] = True
298	        return emit(result, EXIT_OK)
299	
300	    by_n = {e["n"]: e for e in offered}
301	    by_n.update({e["n"].lstrip("0"): e for e in offered})   # accept `1` as well as `01`
302	    names = catalog_names(catalog)
303	
304	    def look_up(tok):
305	        hit = by_n.get(tok)
306	        if hit is not None:
307	            return hit
308	        # Not a menu number -- fall back to name/ID matching, so a user who typed the assay
309	        # instead of picking a number is not punished for it.
310	        match = resolve_assays([tok], names)[0]
311	        if not match["supported"]:
312	            return None
313	        return next((e for e in offered if e["assay_id"] == match["assay_id"]), None)
314	
315	    def try_split(tokens):
316	        hits, bad = [], []
317	        for tok in tokens:
318	            hit = look_up(tok)
319	            if hit is None:
320	                bad.append(tok)
321	            elif hit["assay_id"] not in [h["assay_id"] for h in hits]:
322	                hits.append(hit)
323	        return hits, bad
324	
325	    # Commas first, because the prompt asks for a comma-separated list and an assay NAME may
326	    # contain spaces -- splitting "Bulk RNA-seq" on whitespace tore it into two invalid tokens.
327	    # Only if that fails completely, and there were no commas, retry on whitespace so that
328	    # "01 02" still works.
329	    result["selected"], result["invalid"] = [], []
330	    comma_tokens = [t.strip() for t in args.select.split(",") if t.strip()]
331	    if not comma_tokens:
332	        result["assay_ids"] = []
333	        result["error"] = "empty selection"
334	        result["template"] = "T3"
335	        return emit(result, EXIT_REFUSED)
336	
337	    selected, invalid = try_split(comma_tokens)
338	    if invalid and "," not in args.select:
339	        ws_selected, ws_invalid = try_split(args.select.split())
340	        if not ws_invalid:
341	            selected, invalid = ws_selected, ws_invalid
342	
343	    result["selected"] = selected
344	    result["invalid"] = invalid
345	    # The only thing the caller should pass onward. Numbers stop here.
346	    result["assay_ids"] = [s["assay_id"] for s in selected]
347	    if invalid or not selected:
348	        result["template"] = "T3"
349	        result["error"] = ("could not resolve: %s" % ", ".join(invalid)) if invalid \
350	            else "nothing selected"
351	        return emit(result, EXIT_REFUSED)
352	
353	    result["ok"] = True
354	    return emit(result, EXIT_OK)
355

357	# --- create -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

359	def cmd_create(args, workspace):
360	    result = {"command": "create", "ok": False}
361	    title = sanitize_title(args.title)
362	    result["title"] = args.title
363	    result["sanitized_title"] = title
364	    if not title:
365	        result["error"] = "the title sanitizes to an empty string"
366	        return emit(result, EXIT_USAGE)
367	
368	    project = workspace / "projects" / title
369	    result["project"] = str(project)
370	    if project.exists():
371	        result["template"] = "T7"
372	        result["error"] = "projects/%s/ already exists; nothing was created or modified" % title
373	        return emit(result, EXIT_REFUSED)
374	
375	    catalog, err = read_assay_map(workspace)
376	    if err:
377	        result["error"] = err
378	        return emit(result, EXIT_USAGE)
379	    assay_map = catalog_names(catalog)
380	
381	    validation = resolve_assays(args.assays, assay_map)
382	    result["assays"] = validation
383	    # Both forms, because either is accepted and the ID is what users tend to type.
384	    result["supported_assays"] = [{"assay": name, "assay_id": aid}
385	                                  for aid, name in sorted(assay_map.items())]
386	    supported = [v["assay_id"] for v in validation if v["supported"]]
387	    if not supported:
388	        result["template"] = "T8"
389	        result["error"] = "none of the requested assays are supported; no project was created"
390	        return emit(result, EXIT_REFUSED)
391	
392	    stamp = workspace / "_templates" / "project"
393	    if not stamp.is_dir():
394	        result["error"] = "project stamp not found at %s" % stamp
395	        return emit(result, EXIT_USAGE)
396	
397	    import shutil
398	    shutil.copytree(str(stamp), str(project))
399	    for aid in supported:
400	        (project / "00_data" / aid / "raw").mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
401	
402	    # Seed _config/ so the user never authors a config from a blank file. Everything derivable is
403	    # filled in; the scientific decisions are left marked <REQUIRED>, because no stage substitutes
404	    # a value for them. Making those decisions is the user's; authoring YAML from a 91-line schema
405	    # is not, and a user reasonably asked why they had to.
406	    seeded = []
407	    config_src = workspace / "_templates" / "config"
408	    scratch = os.environ.get("GARS_SCRATCH",
409	                             "/gpfs/scratch/%s/gars-work" % os.environ.get("USER", "USER"))
410	    values = {"{{project_title}}": title, "{{work_dir}}": "%s/%s" % (scratch, title)}
411	    for aid in supported:
412	        src = config_src / (aid + ".yaml")
413	        if src.is_file():
414	            text = src.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
415	            for k, v in values.items():
416	                text = text.replace(k, v)
417	            (project / "_config" / (aid + ".yaml")).write_text(text, encoding="utf-8")
418	            seeded.append("_config/" + aid + ".yaml")
419	    # The Nextflow executor config and the scheduler descriptor (decision 0039) are seeded
420	    # together: one says how Nextflow submits each process, the other how GARS submits the
421	    # job that runs Nextflow. A project that deletes the descriptor gets Slurm's built-in
422	    # defaults, so the pair stays optional-by-deletion rather than fragile.
423	    for name in ("nextflow.slurm.config", "executor.yaml"):
424	        src = config_src / name
425	        if src.is_file() and supported:
426	            shutil.copy2(str(src), str(project / "_config" / name))
427	            seeded.append("_config/" + name)
428	    result["config_seeded"] = seeded
429	
430	    result["created"] = supported
431	    result["template_version"] = template_version(workspace)
432	    result["ok"] = True
433	    return emit(result, EXIT_OK)
434	
435	
436	# --- inspect ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
437	
438	def cmd_inspect(args, workspace):
439	    """Read-only. Writes nothing, so the agent can show counts and ask before any link exists."""
440	    result = {"command": "inspect", "ok": False, "assay_id": args.assay, "source": args.source}
441	    source = Path(args.source)
442	    if not source.is_dir():
443	        result["template"] = "T5"
444	        result["error"] = "not a directory: %s" % source
445	        return emit(result, EXIT_REFUSED)
446	
447	    kind = ws.input_kind(args.assay)
448	    result["input_kind"] = kind
449	    raw, other = find_raw(source, kind)
450	    result["raw_file_count"] = len(raw)
451	    result["excluded_file_count"] = len(other)
452	    result["excluded_examples"] = other[:5]
453	    if not raw:
454	        result["template"] = "T5"
455	        result["error"] = ("no per-sample directories at the top level of %s" % source
456	                           if kind == "sample_dir"
457	                           else "no raw NGS files at the top level of %s" % source)
458	        return emit(result, EXIT_REFUSED)
459	
460	    units, layout, problems = derive_units(raw, args.sample_id_pattern, kind)
461	    if problems:
462	        result["template"] = "T5"
463	        result["error"] = ("cannot derive sample IDs: %d entr%s do not match the expected "
464	                           "convention" % (len(problems), "y" if len(problems) == 1 else "ies"))
465	        result["unmatched_examples"] = problems[:5]
466	        result["convention"] = ("<sample>/ or <sample>.tar.gz, one per sample"
467	                                if kind == "sample_dir"
468	                                else "<sample>_S<n>[_L<lane>]_R<1|2>_<nnn>.fastq.gz")
469	        return emit(result, EXIT_REFUSED)
470	    if layout == "mixed":
471	        result["template"] = "T5"
472	        result["error"] = "mixed/incomplete pairing: some sample-lane units have no R2"
473	        result["unpaired"] = ["%s %s" % k for k, v in sorted(units.items()) if "2" not in v][:10]
474	        return emit(result, EXIT_REFUSED)
475	
476	    result["sample_ids"] = sorted({s for s, _ in units})
477	    result["sample_count"] = len(result["sample_ids"])
478	    result["sample_lane_units"] = len(units)
479	    result["layout"] = layout
480	    # So the agent can state the cost of a full integrity check without computing it itself.
481	    total = sum((source / n).stat().st_size for n in raw if (source / n).is_file())
482	    if kind == "sample_dir":
483	        total = sum(f.stat().st_size
484	                    for n in raw for f in (source / n).rglob("*") if f.is_file()) or total
485	    result["total_bytes"] = total
486	    result["total_gb"] = round(total / 1e9, 1)
487	    result["full_check_estimate_min"] = max(1, int(round(total / 130e6 / 60)))
488	    result["ok"] = True
489	    return emit(result, EXIT_OK)
490

492	# --- link ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
493	
494	def cmd_link(args, workspace):
495	    result = {"command": "link", "ok": False, "assay_id": args.assay, "source": args.source}
496	    project = Path(args.project)
497	    raw_dir = project / "00_data" / args.assay / "raw"
498	    if not raw_dir.is_dir():
499	        result["error"] = "no raw/ directory at %s; run create first" % raw_dir
500	        return emit(result, EXIT_USAGE)
501	
502	    source = Path(args.source)
503	    kind = ws.input_kind(args.assay)
504	    raw, _ = find_raw(source, kind)
505	    if not raw:
506	        result["template"] = "T5"
507	        result["error"] = ("no per-sample directories at the top level of %s" % source
508	                           if kind == "sample_dir"
509	                           else "no raw NGS files at the top level of %s" % source)
510	        return emit(result, EXIT_REFUSED)
511	
512	    existing = list(raw_dir.iterdir())
513	    if existing and not args.force:
514	        result["error"] = ("%s already holds %d entries; refusing to re-link. Stage 00 never "
515	                           "narrows an existing project." % (raw_dir, len(existing)))
516	        return emit(result, EXIT_FAILURE)
517	
518	    linked, broken = [], []
519	    for name in raw:
520	        dest = raw_dir / name
521	        if dest.exists() or dest.is_symlink():
522	            dest.unlink()
523	        os.symlink(str((source / name).resolve()), str(dest))
524	        # A sample_dir link points at a directory, which is not is_file(). What matters either
525	        # way is that the link resolves to something that exists.
526	        (linked if dest.exists() else broken).append(name)
527	
528	    result["linked"] = len(linked)
529	    result["broken"] = broken
530	    if broken:
531	        result["error"] = "%d symlink(s) do not resolve" % len(broken)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Stage 00 — create a project and register its raw data.

The deterministic core of `00_initialize_project`. The contract orchestrates; this computes.
See docs/decisions/0011-deterministic-artifacts-in-stages-00-01.md for why.

This script decides what is TRUE. It never prompts, never links without being told the user
confirmed, and never invents a sample ID it cannot derive. The agent decides what to say and
when to stop.

Stdlib only, and verified on stock python 3.6.8: stages 00 and 01 must run with no conda
environment, unlike stage 02.

The four subcommands are the contract's own phases, so a conversation turn sits between each:

    assays    steps 3-6    offer the supported assays; resolve a selection -> backs T3
    create    step  7      sanitize the title, validate assays, copy the stamp
    inspect   step  9      read-only scan of one source directory   -> backs T4a
    link      step  12     symlink one assay's raw files            -> backs T4b
    finalize  steps 14-19  metadata, placeholders, exit gate        -> backs T6 / T9

Every subcommand emits a single JSON object on stdout. Exit codes:

    0  ok
    1  failure; report and stop (T9)
    2  refused; the JSON's `template` field names which reply to send (T5 / T7 / T8)
    3  usage or precondition error

Note on cost: `finalize` defaults to `--integrity quick` -- resolves, non-empty, gzip magic --
because at this stage EVERY registered file would be verified, including the ones the user is
about to exclude at the 00 -> 01 gate. Deep verification of the files that will actually be
analysed belongs to stage 01, which is the first moment the included subset exists. `--integrity
full` is still available here and still honest about what it did: the mode is stamped into the
project's HISTORY.md, never assumed.
"""

import argparse
import csv
import datetime
import json
import os
import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
import integrity            # noqa: E402  -- one home for the integrity rule
import workspace as ws     # noqa: E402  -- one home for the template version

RAW_SUFFIXES = (".fastq.gz", ".fq.gz", ".fastq", ".fq")
FILES_HEADER = ["sample_id", "lane", "fastq_1", "fastq_2"]
BCL2FASTQ = re.compile(r"^(?P<sample>.+?)_S\d+_(?:L(?P<lane>\d+)_)?R(?P<read>[12])_\d+\."
                       r"(?:fastq|fq)(?:\.gz)?$")

EXIT_OK, EXIT_FAILURE, EXIT_REFUSED, EXIT_USAGE = 0, 1, 2, 3


def emit(result, code):
    json.dump(result, sys.stdout, indent=2, sort_keys=True)
    sys.stdout.write("\n")
    return code


# --- shared -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

def sanitize_title(title):
    """Contract: keep [A-Za-z0-9_-]; space -> _; drop the rest; collapse _; strip leading/trailing
    _ and -."""
    s = title.replace(" ", "_")
    s = "".join(c for c in s if re.match(r"[A-Za-z0-9_-]", c))
    s = re.sub(r"_+", "_", s)
    return s.strip("_-")


def read_assay_map(workspace):
    """Parse the Assay / Assay ID columns of the FIRST table headed `| Assay | Assay ID |`.

    Binding to that header matters: the file holds a second table (Skill requirements) whose
    first two columns are Skill / Python. Reading every pipe-prefixed line accepted `rnaseq-de`
    as an assay and created a directory named `(unpinned)` from the Python column.
    """
    path = workspace / "_references" / "assay_stage_skill_map.md"
    if not path.is_file():
        return None, "assay map not found at %s" % path

    catalog, in_table = {}, False
    for line in path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
        stripped = line.strip()
        if not stripped.startswith("|"):
            if in_table:
                break          # the table ended; never read past it
            continue
        cells = [c.strip() for c in stripped.strip("|").split("|")]
        if len(cells) < 2:
            continue
        if not in_table:
            if cells[0] == "Assay" and cells[1] == "Assay ID":
                in_table = True
            continue
        if set("".join(cells[:2])) <= set("-: "):
            continue           # the header separator row
        name, aid = cells[0], cells[1]
        entry = catalog.setdefault(aid, {"assay": name, "substages": []})
        # One row per sub-stage, in the order the map lists them -- that order IS the pipeline.
        if len(cells) >= 5 and cells[3]:
            entry["substages"].append({"substage": cells[3], "skill": cells[4]})

    if not catalog:
        return None, "assay map has no table headed `| Assay | Assay ID |`"
    return catalog, None


def catalog_names(catalog):
    """{assay_id: display name} -- what the matching and placeholder code needs."""
    return {aid: e["assay"] for aid, e in catalog.items()}


def menu(catalog):
    """The offer list. Numbers are PRESENTATION ONLY.

    They are assigned from a deterministic sort of the Assay IDs and are regenerated on every
    call, so the numbering handed out is always the numbering `--select` resolves against. They
    are never written to disk, never recorded in HISTORY.md, and never used as a directory name:
    add an assay and `02` becomes a different thing, so a persisted number would silently rot.
    The Assay ID is the durable identifier and the only one that leaves this function.
    """
    return [{"n": "%02d" % i, "assay": catalog[aid]["assay"], "assay_id": aid,
             "substages": catalog[aid]["substages"]}
            for i, aid in enumerate(sorted(catalog), start=1)]


def normalize_assay(text):
    """Case-fold and drop every non-alphanumeric character.

    `rnaseq-bulk`, `rnaseq_bulk`, `RNAseq Bulk` and `rnaseq bulk` all normalise to `rnaseqbulk`;
    `Bulk RNA-seq` and `bulk rna seq` both to `bulkrnaseq`. This is normalisation, NOT fuzzy
    matching -- no edit distance, no substring, no stemming. Two different assays cannot collide
    unless their names differ only in punctuation, which `resolve_assays` refuses outright rather
    than guessing between.

    The strict version of this rejected `rnaseq-bulk` -- one character away from the Assay ID it
    obviously meant -- and told the user only that "Bulk RNA-seq" was supported, without ever
    showing the ID. Refusing a punctuation variant is not safety, it is a dead end.
    """
    return "".join(c for c in text.lower() if c.isalnum())


def resolve_assays(requested, assay_map):
    """Match each request against the Assay column or the Assay ID column, after normalisation.

    Returns one entry per request. An unmatched request is reported, never resolved to a
    neighbour: the point of refusing is that a wrong assay silently creates the wrong pipeline.
    """
    index = {}
    for aid, name in assay_map.items():
        for form in (aid, name):
            index.setdefault(normalize_assay(form), set()).add(aid)

    out = []
    for req in requested:
        key = normalize_assay(req)
        hits = index.get(key, set())
        if len(hits) == 1:
            out.append({"requested": req, "assay_id": sorted(hits)[0], "supported": True})
        elif len(hits) > 1:
            out.append({"requested": req, "assay_id": None, "supported": False,
                        "ambiguous_between": sorted(hits),
                        "note": "matches more than one assay; name it by Assay ID"})
        else:
            out.append({"requested": req, "assay_id": None, "supported": False})
    return out


def template_version(workspace):
    return ws.template_version(workspace)


# A Space Ranger output tree may arrive as a directory or as a tarball of one; the pipeline
# accepts either (spatialvi docs/usage.md).
SAMPLE_DIR_SUFFIXES = (".tar.gz", ".tgz")


def find_raw(source, kind="fastq"):
    """Raw input at the TOP LEVEL only. Never descends -- the contract forbids searching.

    `fastq`: files with an NGS suffix. `sample_dir`: one directory (or tarball of one) per
    sample, which is how spatial data arrives -- there are no FASTQs to see.
    """
    raw, other = [], []
    for p in sorted(source.iterdir()):
        if kind == "sample_dir":
            is_input = p.is_dir() or p.name.endswith(SAMPLE_DIR_SUFFIXES)
        else:
            if not p.is_file() and not p.is_symlink():
                continue
            is_input = p.name.endswith(RAW_SUFFIXES)
        (raw if is_input else other).append(p.name)
    return raw, other


def derive_units(filenames, pattern=None, kind="fastq"):
    """Group filenames into (sample_id, lane) units.

    Returns (units, layout, problems). `pattern` overrides the bcl2fastq convention and must
    provide named groups `sample` and `read`, optionally `lane` -- it is how the contract feeds
    back an answer the user gave when filenames do not match the convention.

    For `sample_dir` there is nothing to parse and nothing to pair: each entry IS a sample, its
    id is the entry name with any tarball suffix removed, and the layout is reported as
    `sample-dir` so callers never apply a pairing rule that has no meaning here.
    """
    if kind == "sample_dir":
        units, problems = {}, []
        for name in filenames:
            sample = name
            for suffix in SAMPLE_DIR_SUFFIXES:
                if sample.endswith(suffix):
                    sample = sample[:-len(suffix)]
                    break
            if not sample:
                problems.append(name)
                continue
            if (sample, "") in units:
                problems.append(name)
                continue
            units[(sample, "")] = {"dir": name}
        return ({}, None, problems) if problems else (units, "sample-dir", [])

    rx = re.compile(pattern) if pattern else BCL2FASTQ
    units, problems = {}, []
    for name in filenames:
        m = rx.match(name)
        if not m:
            problems.append(name)
            continue
        gd = m.groupdict()
        sample = gd.get("sample")
        lane = gd.get("lane") or ""
        read = gd.get("read") or "1"
        if not sample:
            problems.append(name)
            continue
        lane = "L%s" % lane if lane and not lane.startswith("L") else lane
        units.setdefault((sample, lane), {})[read] = name

    if problems:
        return {}, None, problems

    r2 = [u for u in units.values() if "2" in u]
    if len(r2) == len(units):
        layout = "paired-end"
    elif not r2:
        layout = "single-end"
    else:
        layout = "mixed"
    return units, layout, []


def units_to_rows(units, assay_id, kind="fastq"):
    """Rows for files.csv, shaped by the assay's input kind (workspace.FILES_HEADERS)."""
    rows = []
    base = "00_data/%s/raw/" % assay_id
    if kind == "sample_dir":
        for (sample, _) in sorted(units):
            rows.append([sample, base + units[(sample, "")]["dir"]])
        return rows
    for (sample, lane) in sorted(units):
        reads = units[(sample, lane)]
        rows.append([sample, lane,
                     base + reads["1"] if "1" in reads else "",
                     base + reads["2"] if "2" in reads else ""])
    return rows


# --- assays ---

def cmd_assays(args, workspace):
    """Offer the supported assays, and resolve a selection back to Assay IDs.

    Two modes, one source of truth. Without --select it returns the menu the agent renders; with
    --select it resolves what the user picked. Both derive from the same `menu()` call, so the
    numbering offered cannot drift from the numbering accepted.

    A selection may name a number (`01`), an Assay ID, or a display name -- whatever the user
    typed. Everything resolves to Assay IDs, and only Assay IDs are returned.
    """
    result = {"command": "assays", "ok": False}
    catalog, err = read_assay_map(workspace)
    if err:
        result["error"] = err
        return emit(result, EXIT_USAGE)

    offered = menu(catalog)
    result["assays"] = offered

    if args.select is None:
        result["ok"] = True
        return emit(result, EXIT_OK)

    by_n = {e["n"]: e for e in offered}
    by_n.update({e["n"].lstrip("0"): e for e in offered})   # accept `1` as well as `01`
    names = catalog_names(catalog)

    def look_up(tok):
        hit = by_n.get(tok)
        if hit is not None:
            return hit
        # Not a menu number -- fall back to name/ID matching, so a user who typed the assay
        # instead of picking a number is not punished for it.
        match = resolve_assays([tok], names)[0]
        if not match["supported"]:
            return None
        return next((e for e in offered if e["assay_id"] == match["assay_id"]), None)

    def try_split(tokens):
        hits, bad = [], []
        for tok in tokens:
            hit = look_up(tok)
            if hit is None:
                bad.append(tok)
            elif hit["assay_id"] not in [h["assay_id"] for h in hits]:
                hits.append(hit)
        return hits, bad

    # Commas first, because the prompt asks for a comma-separated list and an assay NAME may
    # contain spaces -- splitting "Bulk RNA-seq" on whitespace tore it into two invalid tokens.
    # Only if that fails completely, and there were no commas, retry on whitespace so that
    # "01 02" still works.
    result["selected"], result["invalid"] = [], []
    comma_tokens = [t.strip() for t in args.select.split(",") if t.strip()]
    if not comma_tokens:
        result["assay_ids"] = []
        result["error"] = "empty selection"
        result["template"] = "T3"
        return emit(result, EXIT_REFUSED)

    selected, invalid = try_split(comma_tokens)
    if invalid and "," not in args.select:
        ws_selected, ws_invalid = try_split(args.select.split())
        if not ws_invalid:
            selected, invalid = ws_selected, ws_invalid

    result["selected"] = selected
    result["invalid"] = invalid
    # The only thing the caller should pass onward. Numbers stop here.
    result["assay_ids"] = [s["assay_id"] for s in selected]
    if invalid or not selected:
        result["template"] = "T3"
        result["error"] = ("could not resolve: %s" % ", ".join(invalid)) if invalid \
            else "nothing selected"
        return emit(result, EXIT_REFUSED)

    result["ok"] = True
    return emit(result, EXIT_OK)


# --- create -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

def cmd_create(args, workspace):
    result = {"command": "create", "ok": False}
    title = sanitize_title(args.title)
    result["title"] = args.title
    result["sanitized_title"] = title
    if not title:
        result["error"] = "the title sanitizes to an empty string"
        return emit(result, EXIT_USAGE)

    project = workspace / "projects" / title
    result["project"] = str(project)
    if project.exists():
        result["template"] = "T7"
        result["error"] = "projects/%s/ already exists; nothing was created or modified" % title
        return emit(result, EXIT_REFUSED)

    catalog, err = read_assay_map(workspace)
    if err:
        result["error"] = err
        return emit(result, EXIT_USAGE)
    assay_map = catalog_names(catalog)

    validation = resolve_assays(args.assays, assay_map)
    result["assays"] = validation
    # Both forms, because either is accepted and the ID is what users tend to type.
    result["supported_assays"] = [{"assay": name, "assay_id": aid}
                                  for aid, name in sorted(assay_map.items())]
    supported = [v["assay_id"] for v in validation if v["supported"]]
    if not supported:
        result["template"] = "T8"
        result["error"] = "none of the requested assays are supported; no project was created"
        return emit(result, EXIT_REFUSED)

    stamp = workspace / "_templates" / "project"
    if not stamp.is_dir():
        result["error"] = "project stamp not found at %s" % stamp
        return emit(result, EXIT_USAGE)

    import shutil
    shutil.copytree(str(stamp), str(project))
    for aid in supported:
        (project / "00_data" / aid / "raw").mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    # Seed _config/ so the user never authors a config from a blank file. Everything derivable is
    # filled in; the scientific decisions are left marked <REQUIRED>, because no stage substitutes
    # a value for them. Making those decisions is the user's; authoring YAML from a 91-line schema
    # is not, and a user reasonably asked why they had to.
    seeded = []
    config_src = workspace / "_templates" / "config"
    scratch = os.environ.get("GARS_SCRATCH",
                             "/gpfs/scratch/%s/gars-work" % os.environ.get("USER", "USER"))
    values = {"{{project_title}}": title, "{{work_dir}}": "%s/%s" % (scratch, title)}
    for aid in supported:
        src = config_src / (aid + ".yaml")
        if src.is_file():
            text = src.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
            for k, v in values.items():
                text = text.replace(k, v)
            (project / "_config" / (aid + ".yaml")).write_text(text, encoding="utf-8")
            seeded.append("_config/" + aid + ".yaml")
    # The Nextflow executor config and the scheduler descriptor (decision 0039) are seeded
    # together: one says how Nextflow submits each process, the other how GARS submits the
    # job that runs Nextflow. A project that deletes the descriptor gets Slurm's built-in
    # defaults, so the pair stays optional-by-deletion rather than fragile.
    for name in ("nextflow.slurm.config", "executor.yaml"):
        src = config_src / name
        if src.is_file() and supported:
            shutil.copy2(str(src), str(project / "_config" / name))
            seeded.append("_config/" + name)
    result["config_seeded"] = seeded

    result["created"] = supported
    result["template_version"] = template_version(workspace)
    result["ok"] = True
    return emit(result, EXIT_OK)


# --- inspect ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

def cmd_inspect(args, workspace):
    """Read-only. Writes nothing, so the agent can show counts and ask before any link exists."""
    result = {"command": "inspect", "ok": False, "assay_id": args.assay, "source": args.source}
    source = Path(args.source)
    if not source.is_dir():
        result["template"] = "T5"
        result["error"] = "not a directory: %s" % source
        return emit(result, EXIT_REFUSED)

    kind = ws.input_kind(args.assay)
    result["input_kind"] = kind
    raw, other = find_raw(source, kind)
    result["raw_file_count"] = len(raw)
    result["excluded_file_count"] = len(other)
    result["excluded_examples"] = other[:5]
    if not raw:
        result["template"] = "T5"
        result["error"] = ("no per-sample directories at the top level of %s" % source
                           if kind == "sample_dir"
                           else "no raw NGS files at the top level of %s" % source)
        return emit(result, EXIT_REFUSED)

    units, layout, problems = derive_units(raw, args.sample_id_pattern, kind)
    if problems:
        result["template"] = "T5"
        result["error"] = ("cannot derive sample IDs: %d entr%s do not match the expected "
                           "convention" % (len(problems), "y" if len(problems) == 1 else "ies"))
        result["unmatched_examples"] = problems[:5]
        result["convention"] = ("<sample>/ or <sample>.tar.gz, one per sample"
                                if kind == "sample_dir"
                                else "<sample>_S<n>[_L<lane>]_R<1|2>_<nnn>.fastq.gz")
        return emit(result, EXIT_REFUSED)
    if layout == "mixed":
        result["template"] = "T5"
        result["error"] = "mixed/incomplete pairing: some sample-lane units have no R2"
        result["unpaired"] = ["%s %s" % k for k, v in sorted(units.items()) if "2" not in v][:10]
        return emit(result, EXIT_REFUSED)

    result["sample_ids"] = sorted({s for s, _ in units})
    result["sample_count"] = len(result["sample_ids"])
    result["sample_lane_units"] = len(units)
    result["layout"] = layout
    # So the agent can state the cost of a full integrity check without computing it itself.
    total = sum((source / n).stat().st_size for n in raw if (source / n).is_file())
    if kind == "sample_dir":
        total = sum(f.stat().st_size
                    for n in raw for f in (source / n).rglob("*") if f.is_file()) or total
    result["total_bytes"] = total
    result["total_gb"] = round(total / 1e9, 1)
    result["full_check_estimate_min"] = max(1, int(round(total / 130e6 / 60)))
    result["ok"] = True
    return emit(result, EXIT_OK)


# --- link ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

def cmd_link(args, workspace):
    result = {"command": "link", "ok": False, "assay_id": args.assay, "source": args.source}
    project = Path(args.project)
    raw_dir = project / "00_data" / args.assay / "raw"
    if not raw_dir.is_dir():
        result["error"] = "no raw/ directory at %s; run create first" % raw_dir
        return emit(result, EXIT_USAGE)

    source = Path(args.source)
    kind = ws.input_kind(args.assay)
    raw, _ = find_raw(source, kind)
    if not raw:
        result["template"] = "T5"
        result["error"] = ("no per-sample directories at the top level of %s" % source
                           if kind == "sample_dir"
                           else "no raw NGS files at the top level of %s" % source)
        return emit(result, EXIT_REFUSED)

    existing = list(raw_dir.iterdir())
    if existing and not args.force:
        result["error"] = ("%s already holds %d entries; refusing to re-link. Stage 00 never "
                           "narrows an existing project." % (raw_dir, len(existing)))
        return emit(result, EXIT_FAILURE)

    linked, broken = [], []
    for name in raw:
        dest = raw_dir / name
        if dest.exists() or dest.is_symlink():
            dest.unlink()
        os.symlink(str((source / name).resolve()), str(dest))
        # A sample_dir link points at a directory, which is not is_file(). What matters either
        # way is that the link resolves to something that exists.
        (linked if dest.exists() else broken).append(name)

    result["linked"] = len(linked)
    result["broken"] = broken
    if broken:
        result["error"] = "%d symlink(s) do not resolve" % len(broken)
        return emit(result, EXIT_FAILURE)
    result["ok"] = True
    return emit(result, EXIT_OK)


# --- finalize -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------

def cmd_finalize(args, workspace):
    result = {"command": "finalize", "ok": False, "assays": {}, "failures": []}
    project = Path(args.project)
    if not project.is_dir():
        result["failures"].append("project does not exist: %s" % project)
        return emit(result, EXIT_USAGE)

    catalog, err = read_assay_map(workspace)
    if err:
        result["failures"].append(err)
        return emit(result, EXIT_USAGE)
    assay_map = catalog_names(catalog)

    data_root = project / "00_data"
    assays = sorted(d.name for d in data_root.iterdir() if d.is_dir())
    if not assays:
        result["failures"].append("no assay directories under 00_data/")
        return emit(result, EXIT_USAGE)

    version = template_version(workspace)
    created = args.date or datetime.date.today().isoformat()
    per_assay = {}

    for aid in assays:
        raw_dir = data_root / aid / "raw"
        names = sorted(p.name for p in raw_dir.iterdir()) if raw_dir.is_dir() else []
        if not names:
            result["failures"].append("%s: raw/ is empty" % aid)
            continue

        kind = ws.input_kind(aid)
        units, layout, problems = derive_units(names, args.sample_id_pattern, kind)
        if problems:
            result["failures"].append("%s: %d linked entr%s do not match the convention"
                                      % (aid, len(problems),
                                         "y" if len(problems) == 1 else "ies"))
            continue
        if layout == "mixed":
            result["failures"].append("%s: pairing is incomplete" % aid)
            continue

        # Source path is DERIVED from the symlinks, not remembered -- the filesystem is the state.
        sources = sorted({os.path.dirname(os.readlink(str(raw_dir / n)))
                          for n in names if (raw_dir / n).is_symlink()})

        rows = units_to_rows(units, aid, kind)
        with ws.atomic_open(data_root / aid / "files.csv",
                            mode=ws.MACHINE_OWNED_MODE) as fh:
            fh.write("# generated by stage 00 — do not edit\n")
            w = csv.writer(fh, lineterminator="\n")
            w.writerow(ws.files_header(aid))
            for r in rows:
                w.writerow(r)

        # files.csv is machine-owned and is always regenerated from raw/.
        # samples.csv is NOT: it is the user's file, and re-running finalize must never destroy a
        # design they have filled in, or an exclusion they expressed by deleting rows. It is
        # written once, on creation, and preserved thereafter. A sample present in raw/ but absent
        # from samples.csv is an exclusion, which is stage 01's business to confirm -- not a gap
        # for this stage to silently fill back in.
        sample_ids = sorted({s for s, _ in units})
        samples_csv = data_root / aid / "samples.csv"
        if samples_csv.exists():
            samples_state = "preserved"
        else:
            samples_state = "created"
            with ws.atomic_open(samples_csv) as fh:
                w = csv.writer(fh, lineterminator="\n")
                w.writerow(ws.design_columns(aid))
                for sid in sample_ids:
                    w.writerow([sid, "", "", ""])

        per_assay[aid] = {"display": assay_map.get(aid, aid), "files": len(names),
                          "samples": len(sample_ids), "units": len(units), "layout": layout,
                          "sources": sources, "samples_csv": samples_state}
        result["assays"][aid] = {k: v for k, v in per_assay[aid].items()}

    if result["failures"]:
        return emit(result, EXIT_FAILURE)

    # -- placeholders
    assay_table = ["| Assay | Assay ID | Data directory | Files | Samples |", "|---|---|---|---|---|"]
    source_rows = ["| Assay ID | Source path | Files linked |", "|---|---|---|"]
    for aid in assays:
        m = per_assay[aid]
        assay_table.append("| %s | %s | `00_data/%s/` | %d | %d |"
                           % (m["display"], aid, aid, m["files"], m["samples"]))
        source_rows.append("| %s | %s | %d |"
                           % (aid, ", ".join("`%s`" % s for s in m["sources"]) or "unknown",
                              m["files"]))

    values = {"{{project_title}}": project.name, "{{created}}": created,
              "{{template_version}}": version, "{{assay_table}}": "\n".join(assay_table),
              "{{source_paths}}": "\n".join(source_rows),
              "{{integrity}}": args.integrity,
              "{{model}}": args.model or "unknown"}
    for fname in ("CONTEXT.md", "HISTORY.md"):
        p = project / fname
        if not p.is_file():
            result["failures"].append("%s is missing; was the stamp copied?" % fname)
            continue
        text = p.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        for k, v in values.items():
            text = text.replace(k, v)
        with ws.atomic_open(p, newline=None) as fh:
            fh.write(text)

    # -- exit gate (step 19)
    gate, checked = [], 0
    for fname in ("CONTEXT.md", "HISTORY.md"):
        if not (project / fname).is_file():
            gate.append("%s does not exist" % fname)
    if not (project / "_config").is_dir():
        gate.append("_config/ does not exist")

    unsubstituted = sorted(str(p.relative_to(project)) for p in project.rglob("*")
                           if p.is_file() and p.suffix == ".md" and "{{" in p.read_text(
                               encoding="utf-8", errors="ignore"))
    if unsubstituted:
        gate.append("unsubstituted placeholder remains in: %s" % ", ".join(unsubstituted))

    for aid in assays:
        f_csv, s_csv = data_root / aid / "files.csv", data_root / aid / "samples.csv"
        frows = [r for r in csv.DictReader(
            [l for l in f_csv.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines() if not l.startswith("#")])]
        srows = list(csv.DictReader(s_csv.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines()))
        if not frows:
            gate.append("%s: files.csv is empty" % aid)
        if not srows:
            gate.append("%s: samples.csv is empty" % aid)
        if per_assay[aid]["samples_csv"] == "created" and \
                len({r["sample_id"] for r in frows}) != len(srows):
            gate.append("%s: %d distinct sample_id in files.csv but %d rows in samples.csv"
                        % (aid, len({r["sample_id"] for r in frows}), len(srows)))
        extra = {r["sample_id"] for r in srows} - {r["sample_id"] for r in frows}
        if extra:
            gate.append("%s: samples.csv names %d sample(s) with no rows in files.csv: %s"
                        % (aid, len(extra), ", ".join(sorted(extra)[:5])))
        if any(not r["sample_id"] for r in frows + srows):
            gate.append("%s: a row has an empty sample_id" % aid)
        if ws.input_kind(aid) == "sample_dir":
            # No pairing to check and nothing to checksum: the unit of input is a directory,
            # and hashing a Space Ranger tree would be checking someone else's output rather
            # than the files GARS registered. What CAN go wrong is a link that resolves to
            # nothing, so that is what is checked.
            for r in frows:
                rel = r.get("spaceranger_dir", "")
                if not rel:
                    gate.append("%s: a row has an empty spaceranger_dir" % aid)
                elif not (project / rel).exists():
                    gate.append("%s: %s does not resolve" % (aid, rel))
            continue
        if per_assay[aid]["layout"] == "paired-end" and any(not r["fastq_2"] for r in frows):
            gate.append("%s: pairing is incomplete in files.csv" % aid)
        to_check = [(r[col], project / r[col])
                    for r in frows for col in ("fastq_1", "fastq_2") if r[col]]
        checked += len(to_check)
        for rel, problem in integrity.check_many(to_check, args.integrity):
            gate.append("%s: %s %s" % (aid, rel, problem))

    if gate:
        result["failures"] = gate
        result["template"] = "T9"
        return emit(result, EXIT_FAILURE)

    result["template_version"] = version
    result["model"] = args.model or "unknown"
    result["created"] = created
    result["integrity"] = {"mode": args.integrity,
                           "files_checked": checked}
    result["ok"] = True
    return emit(result, EXIT_OK)


# --- main ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

def main(argv=None):
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.splitlines()[0])
    ap.add_argument("--workspace", type=Path, default=Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent,
                    help="workspace root (default: the parent of _system/)")
    sub = ap.add_subparsers(dest="cmd")

    a = sub.add_parser("assays", help="offer the supported assays; resolve a selection")
    a.add_argument("--select", default=None,
                   help="comma-separated menu numbers, Assay IDs or names; omit to just list")

    c = sub.add_parser("create", help="sanitize the title, validate assays, copy the stamp")
    c.add_argument("--title", required=True)
    c.add_argument("--assays", required=True, nargs="+",
                   help="assay names or Assay IDs, as the user gave them")

    i = sub.add_parser("inspect", help="read-only scan of one source directory")
    i.add_argument("--assay", required=True)
    i.add_argument("--source", required=True)
    i.add_argument("--sample-id-pattern", default=None,
                   help="regex with named groups sample/read[/lane], when filenames do not match "
                        "the bcl2fastq convention and the user has said how to read them")

    l = sub.add_parser("link", help="symlink one assay's raw files")
    l.add_argument("--project", required=True)
    l.add_argument("--assay", required=True)
    l.add_argument("--source", required=True)
    l.add_argument("--force", action="store_true", help="re-link a populated raw/ (never routine)")

    f = sub.add_parser("finalize", help="metadata, placeholders, exit gate")
    f.add_argument("--project", required=True)
    f.add_argument("--date", default=None, help="creation date; defaults to today")
    f.add_argument("--sample-id-pattern", default=None)
    f.add_argument("--model",  default="unknown",
                   help="the exact model id of the agent executing this stage. The model is part "
                        "of the toolchain that produced the project, so HISTORY.md records it "
                        "beside the template version; `unknown` is an honest value, a fabricated "
                        "one is not (decision 0024).")
    f.add_argument("--integrity", choices=("full", "quick", "skip"), default="quick",
                   help="quick (default): resolves, non-empty, gzip magic. full: additionally "
                        "decompress every .gz -- O(data), and at this stage it would verify every "
                        "registered file including ones the user is about to exclude. skip: "
                        "resolution and non-emptiness only.")

    args = ap.parse_args(argv)
    if not args.cmd:
        ap.print_help(sys.stderr)
        return EXIT_USAGE
    return {"assays": cmd_assays, "create": cmd_create, "inspect": cmd_inspect,
            "link": cmd_link, "finalize": cmd_finalize}[args.cmd](args, args.workspace)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())
